selection: Exact current logical/discharge closure for both changed public interfaces; proof-only suppliers checked at actual relevant uses. Target carriers have no aliases. No interface-changed consumer omitted.

reviews.review: 1.1 constructs pressure coefficients directly from L1 u tensor u; 2.1 is a frequency identity. The local H^{-r} extension is consistent with those coefficients and adds no pressure regularity. Existence and weak identities used in F1 are preserved.

F3 applies the unchanged global existence theorem at d=3 and nu=mu/rho0; F2 and 3.1 use exactly its original initial/restart energy clauses. No physical postulate, SI scaling or applicability condition changes.

Uses only the unchanged periodic weak existence/weak-smooth conclusions, with existing Countable and Dependent Choice and unit-torus rescaling. No new pressure, thermal, empirical or global-regularity claim follows.

The mechanical branch still supplies velocity and kinetic dissipation only; the thermal branch remains separately postulated, with no temperature inference or coupled energy law introduced by the mathematical repairs.

The compactness/existence hypotheses and lack of unrestricted regularity/uniqueness remain exactly as summarized in F1-F3 and 1.1-2.1. The proof-only representative correction does not alter those hypotheses.

F4 is used for fixed-mode nonlinear coefficient bounds in 2.2; those follow directly from the same L1 coefficient estimate. Galerkin fields in 1.1 are smooth, where the extended P agrees with the original L2 projection. F3 and 2.2/3.2 use the actual coefficient-defined weakly continuous map, now retained unchanged by the compactness draft. All global, initial and restart claims are preserved.

F1/F5 and all three proof steps use the same weakly continuous representative, weak identity and all-time energy inequality. Neither the nonlinearity estimate nor initial entropy convention occurs in the comparison. All Countable/Dependent Choice qualifications remain.
Entire frontmatter-only placement page read; inventory occurrence adds no mathematical assertion.

The two-state profile and initial data are bounded, so state/flux and polynomial entropy compositions are integrable up to zero. Proof 1.1 explicitly includes the initial cutoff and 1.2 proves the positive residual. Fan comparison and nonuniqueness limitations are unchanged.

Its entire Statement and 1.1-3.1 concern interior regular distributions on open Q and null-hyperplane reassignment. It uses no test meeting an initial boundary, so no new initial integrability premise is required.

Its entire Definition uses C1 fluxes, endpoint Jacobians and Rankine-Hugoniot algebra only, with no initial-value tests or entropy compositions. Its arbitrary open state-domain generalization is self-contained and preserved.
Its entire Definition uses local side C1 extensions, interface traces and a state domain; no initial-value weak or entropy test occurs. Open time sets and all side hypotheses remain valid.
The profile and data lie in [a,b], so all state/flux/entropy compositions are bounded on compact initial supports. The explicit strong local trace estimate and the Riemann supplier remain unchanged.

The profile and data take only a,b off null sets. Every smooth entropy and compatible flux is bounded on [b,a], giving all initial-boundary integrals; F1/F4 and 1.1 retain the exact scalar Riemann and initial formulations.
F1 and proof 1.1-3.1 concern the interior entropy residual and its sign. No initial term occurs; the original C1 side extensions and locally integrable compositions remain sufficient.

Uniform finite range bounds every state/flux/entropy composition on initial-boundary compact supports. Proof 3.1 derives the initial-data bound and convergence; the draft adds the explicit thin-time-strip argument for passing to tests nonzero at zero. Public Statement is unchanged.

The shock, fan and constant profiles take values in the compact interval joining a,b. Continuous state, flux and entropy compositions are bounded there, and hence integrable on compact supports up to zero. Initial data have the same finite range. Proof 3.1/4.2/5.1/6.1 already performs the required initial-strip arguments. Lax use F4/1.2 is the scalar endpoint inequality on O=R.

F2 and proof 1.1-3.1 use compactly supported interior tests in open I x Omega; residual and plane measure definitions do not involve prescribed t=0 data. Initial integrability clarification leaves every assertion unchanged.
Entire frontmatter-only placement page read; inventory occurrence adds no mathematical assertion.
